back: Activities that assess whether a solution has achieved the desired business results, by comparing actual results with expected ones.
Evaluate solution performance; determine solution evaluation approach; evaluate acceptance results and address defects; obtain solution acceptance for release.
When a go/no-go or release decision is needed; shortly after going into operation; well after, to see whether business goals were met.
Where more functionality would not justify the extra effort. Evaluation can justify ending early.
When and how a solution will be evaluated, which metrics will be used, whether the data can be collected, and who is responsible.

front: Why define the evaluation approach early?
back: Some metrics need data the product would not otherwise capture. Left late, it is costly or impossible to obtain.
A set of quantifiable measures used to evaluate a solution or business.
A metric, usually set by executives, used to judge progress toward the organization's goals.

front: Two kinds of metric in the evaluation approach
back: Metrics for acceptance during or shortly after development; metrics to judge later whether business value was delivered.

front: A metric is too costly to collect
back: Use a less costly, next-best alternative.

front: Evaluate Acceptance Results and Address Defects
back: Deciding what to do with the results of comparing the acceptance criteria against the solution.
Actual: the pass or fail results from testing. Evaluated: those results analyzed for cause, cost and business impact, with recommendations.

front: Testers vs business analysts in acceptance
back: Testers determine pass or fail. Analysts assess severity, root cause, risk and impact, and recommend what to do.
A workaround; a modification to the product; an adjustment to the measurement; technical investigation; communication to users.
Determining the cause and size of the difference between the expected value and actual performance.

front: How does a traceability matrix help with defects?
back: It shows which business objective a failed feature traces to, and so how much the defect matters.
A test of the solution through the activities of a typical working day.

front: A story fails its acceptance criteria (adaptive)
back: The story can be rejected and returned to the backlog to be reprioritized.
Facilitating a decision on whether to release all or part of a solution, and handing over knowledge of the product, its risks and workarounds.

front: Four bases for a release decision
back: Acceptable results; organizational readiness; transition activities complete; remaining risks and workarounds accepted.
Release, partial release, delay, or disapprove.
The stakeholders accountable for the product. The business analyst facilitates.
A time after release during which the development team is responsible for fixing defects.

front: Best setting for a release decision
back: A facilitated workshop, so all stakeholders hear the reasoning.
Often the product owner's verbal approval at the demonstration that the work meets the definition of done.
Evaluating a solution in operation to determine whether it is delivering the business value intended.
A quantified output of a product: throughput, cost reduction, users, revenue, sales, customer satisfaction.
Performance after release minus the baseline before release.
An indirect measure used when the objective itself cannot be measured: task duration, response time, error counts.

front: Four typical reasons business value is missed
back: Technical causes; business practices or constraints; resistance to the product; workarounds invented by users.
The comparison of expected with actual value, with reasons. Feeds decisions to enhance, maintain, replace or discontinue the product.
A growth-share matrix placing products by market growth and market share.

front: Portfolio matrix: high growth, high share
back: The most beneficial products (stars).

front: Portfolio matrix: low growth, high share
back: A dependable income stream (cash cows).

front: How does solution evaluation close the loop?
back: Its findings may trigger a new needs assessment.
People; data; production environment; transition and production support; cultural.
Go: release permitted, in whole or in part. No-go: release delayed or disapproved.
